title: Still not as useful as Palm To-Do or Microsoft Tasks
body: Apple still hasn’t figured out how to do a repeating reminder that repeats the interval “after completion,” instead of just a straight, unalterable interval.  For instance, if you want to do your car’s oil change every 3 months: say you complete it in December, and so the next due date is in March.  However, if you don’t actually do your March oil change until May, Apple Reminders schedules your next oil change in June, which doesn’t make any sense.  In Palm To-Do and Microsoft Tasks, you can have that 3-month interval automatically reset at the completion date (in our example, then, the new due date would be set to August) which makes much more sense.  Also, if you create a repeating reminder that is some hourly interval (like for medication) and you have an end date for the repetition, this app still hasn’t figured out how to stop reminding you after the end date!  Very annoying!!😖😡

title: Helping me stay on track so I don’t forget
body:
The set up was a little bit challenging for me at first.  But once I got the hang of it, it has been running well! 
I was recently given medications for multiple times a day and I wanted to be sure I took them on time so my body could metabolize them like clockwork.  Im not huge on taking pills, and this was important, to be honest, with pain killers and other meds and supplements.  Once I set this all up to alarm me to take my meds, it’s been great!!  And sometimes I use it for day to day stuff that pop up that are out of routine and I don’t want to wander to procrastination so it helps me out!  I have tried to get my husband to use this too for the same reasons.  But in case anyone reads this, it does connect to your calendar app so when you look over the calendar it’s listed there too!  It’s nice to look back on when I started checking off all my reminders when they happen, it’s rewarding to see Ive been pretty successful!  I’d be a bit of a clock watcher without this and if I get busy, The time can easily get away from me!  Sound familiar?  So try this out!!  It helps to not be a time chaser, and as long as you’re near your device you’ll know Whrn it’s time to do what it is you needed to do.

title: Missing start time
body: “Remind me in a month” shouldn’t result in a reminder that I see until the next month.  Reminders should only show what is available to do, not the totality of what’s there.  Which is to say, Reminders is nice, but neolithic and the smallest amount of thought would make the app useful for more than 20 items.  As is, it’s not useful.  A “Filter Available” that shows things between start time and now, based on location, etc, would be amazing… and it’s a stones throw from possible, but maddening.  If “Filter Available” also included items that have a location that also aligns with what’s in my calendar, that would be over the top useful.  The pieces are there, but someone is missing the UX chops to make this happen.

title: You Really Don’t Need Anything More Sophisticated
body:
Its UX is simple but visually appealing. It is a native app tightly integrated into the ecosystem. It gives you the ever-useful Kanban view, lists, and tagging to address 80% of “advanced” use cases for work management workflows. 

The only reason it doesn’t get 5 stars for me is lack of an API or more robust Shortcuts intents to make up for an API across all Apple platforms. 

Bonus points if it had a web version to use in team scenarios where there is a Green bubble in the mix.

title: Not Smart
body: I use the Reminder app all the time, often when my hands are full or while I’m driving, and I’m constantly amazed at the lack of smarts. Siri often get things wrong, and after many years is still unable by voice to edit or reschedule reminders once I’ve created them. Even without artificial intelligence, I can imagine a simple system whereby, even five or six or seven years ago, we should have been able to tell Siri we want to edit a reminder, be asked which one, have Siri suggest verbally which one it thinks we’re talking about, and then give us prompts about the location, time, etc. that we might want to edit. Instead, I’m left floundering when trying to edit, and instead, I am forced to make a new reminder that repeats the old one, but at the time or day, I wanted to move it to. Then, when I’m back at my computer or able to look at my phone again, I have to remember to delete the old one. Not smart.

My daily meds?  I never miss them anymore.  Thanks, Apple.

title: Works as expected
body:
I don’t really know what to mention about this iOS feature other than it works as expected and is obviously easy to get notifications across your Apple devices. 
I do prefer to save my reminders into my outlook account, enabling me to receive my reminders both on my Apple, Windows, and Amazon Echo Show device that sits in my kitchen which I pretty much only use for calendar reminders. 
I like that when saved into my outlook account I can select to have the Amazon device announce my reminder out loud, so if I ignore my phone I’ll hear anything important on that device.
It would be great if Apple could work out a deal with Amazon so it plays the reminders on their devices, but I understand they’re competing for market share of similar products, hence why they aren’t cross-compatible.

title: Slight Complaint (And Feedback)
body:
Hi Reminders!!! This app really helps me remind myself what to do!!! 

With the specific dates I set up appointments, and with the times I can remember to make certain calls and do things I’m supposed to. 

The only complaint I have is that there is no option for repeating dates; having more than one set day. 

And a specific weekday’s option!! (Like Momday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, etc). 

It’d be so much easier if you could have reminders for thise certain days, so you don’t have to make several seperate reminders.

Please consider my feedback!!! Thank you so migh for reading!!


Hi Reminders!!! Update, the app has been helping me really much. 

The only thing that annoys me is that I get reminders in the middle of the night

I set multiple and they bother me consistently when I’m trying to sleep.

I wish there was a “Skip Today” option, where you don’t have to constantly manually reset each setting for the reminder

The “Skip Today” feature can keep everything intact about the reminder, but saves it for another day. So you don’t have to reset every aspect of it all over again.

I hope this helps!!! Thank you so much for creating this app!!

title: Excellent integration
body: The integration across platforms, and with Siri, is outstanding. I have been at the grocery store and remembered something I needed to do for work; adding it to my “work” list meant I saw it when I opened that list on my laptop. I’ve been on my laptop and remembered I needed to get Milk; I added it to our “Shared Shopping” list for my wife to get. I’ve been working on the yard and remembered I needed to check on a financial issue; I quickly spoke into my watch “Remind me at 5 O’clock to check my card statement,” and my phone alerted me two hours later to knock that out. And probably the best part: my phone completely bricked a couple years ago, and when I got a new one ALL of my reminders—including specific anniversary gifts planned for months down the road—were ready and available.

title: Suggestion: Connect Calendar And Reminder
body:
Calendar and Reminder should automatically share/ sync with each other, or at least be capable of it. They’re already in a very similar space. They should be sharing data/ events/ plans/ todos. Idk specifically how it would work, but one suggestion would be to link/ sync them whenever a Reminder with date/time data/events/items are created. If there’s no date/time for a list or item, then don’t treat it as a Calendar event. If date/ time is attached to a Reminder list or list item, then ask the user to add it to their Calendar.

Maybe this is already a thing, but I’ve looked and didn’t find it.

title: It was there all along
body:
This app has completely changed how I manage my daily life. The reminders feature is simple, clean, and actually works exactly the way I need it to. I love that it’s not overloaded with unnecessary options—just straightforward, reliable alerts that help me stay on top of things without feeling overwhelmed.
What I appreciate most is how intuitive it feels. The design is minimal and beautiful, the colored dots make it easy to glance and know what’s coming up, and the “Don’t forget” nudge is a nice touch that feels personal rather than pushy.
If you’ve been looking for a reminders app that just gets out of your way and does the job beautifully, this is it. Highly recommend

title: Good but needs better automatic category help and linking to events
body:
Reminders works well as a basic tool but I find I end up with way too many reminders and would like more smart assistance in a clear way to prioritize them/categorize them/work through them, and ultimately to easily identify stale reminders that should be removed. 

I would like to be able to quickly link the reminders to an Emails. 
For emails this would be better integrated into the need for follow up email or creating multiple new reminders that originates from (and have a link to) the original email. 

Reminders could be linked to an upcoming calendar event. (Not just calendar events in their own right ) This would help organization.

For reminders related to a calendar event the time deadline for a reminder is not necessarily just the final  meeting event time. It is usually before that final time, but the reminder should also allow a logical link to that final event. 

It would also help to have better automated suggestions on classification of reminders based on words used in creating the reminder, and existing/historical reminder classifications.

title: Enjoying the New Power Features
body:
As someone who is extremely task-driven, iOS Reminders has become the command center of my day. The integration with Microsoft To Do is outstanding — I can see both my personal reminders (native iOS) and work tasks (via Microsoft To Do) together in the Reminders app, which keeps everything in one streamlined view.

The visibility of Reminders directly on the iOS Calendar has been a game changer for my time management. Being able to see tasks and scheduled events in one place has significantly improved how I prioritize my day.

I also love the new Urgent alarm feature. The stronger alert at reminder time makes a real difference when something truly needs attention.

My one wish: I’d love a similar alarm-style option for Calendar events — especially for meetings synced from Google Calendar. Standard alerts are fine, but an actual “alarm” at meeting start time would be even better.

Excited to see how Apple Intelligence could be leveraged to enhance this app. It’s already powerful — and has real potential to become indispensable for productivity-focused users.

title: Agree with other reviews - The best reminder app
body:
Since this is Apple’s native Reminders app, it integrates seamlessly with other Apple applications. No matter how you prefer to organize your reminders, the app offers flexible features such as lists, sections, and nested subtasks that are easy to customize to fit your unique needs. One feature I recently discovered is the ability to attach photos to individual reminder items. I now use this function to add images of my online shopping purchases, which helps me keep track of what I already own—essentially turning the app into my digital closet.

That said, I wish the app did not automatically crop photos, as this makes it difficult to view complete outfits. It would be much more helpful if photo sizes remained consistent across devices and view modes, allowing users to see the full image clearly.

I love the Reminders app. I let go of paid apps and had committed to using Apple apps productivity apps together. They are seamless and I’m down for that. However, the Subtask function could use a bit of improving. 

For example, it would be nice when viewing a Subtask outside of its original task you could see the original task the Subtask is related too. When you go to the details of the Subtask you can’t tell where it belongs. Also would be nice if we could see the title of the original task and be able to click on it to go directly to the original task. That way you can manage all of the tasks at one time.

title: ADHD help
body: So glad I learned about this app. I realized years ago, back when PalmPilots were the newest technology, that I needed a calendar that yells at me. Now I have a to-do list that does that as well. I schedule tasks for reminders to come at the times that work best for me. Some I want to come at a specific time. Others I want to have showing when I’m ready to start my day. It’s easy to change the date and/or time for things I didn’t get to, or decide I just don’t have the bandwidth for right then, so the reminder doesn’t keep nagging me. The update that included my scheduled to-dos on my calendar makes it even easier. I can now see my entire day, including how the repeated daily tasks will fit into my schedule, and check them off as I complete them.

body:

If I look at the All view the reminders are no longer sorted by my chosen sort order which makes no sense at all and adds friction to my use. 

I would like to delete some of the canned views as I have no use for them but I can’t. 

Apple can contact me to work out these and other kinks.

title: No “Repeat After Completion”
body:
No “repeat after completion” - Still missing a basic feature
Apple Reminders is easy to use, but it’s missing a very basic function: repeating a task after you mark it complete. There is no “repeat after completion” option anywhere in the app or in iOS, and Apple has never addressed why. If you need reminders that recur based on when you actually do something (like medication every 30 days), this app still can’t do it. Very disappointing for something built into iOS.

title: Takes forever to sync
body: Making simple changes such as completing a recurring task or moving it in sequence can take up to 20 minutes to update - not just across devices but on the device being utilized itself. Many times a change will be made and it will reverse itself until it syncs, so if you make several edits you have to walk away from the device to let it catch up or you’ll have a mess. Apple asked me months ago to make test cases and we did live screen shots and recordings etc. I spent hours doing their QA work for them - and nothing. They confirmed it was a common complaint, but I’ve got 26.1 and it’s still not working - AND now search is broken. I will search for something I know is there and other things will return. I have to then manually go through the whole list to find it.

title: “Front Burner” Tasks
body:
As a SBO and professional organizer, I’m always looking for various ways to aid in time management for both myself and my clients. 

As a woman with FULL-ON, lifelong ADHD, not everything works for me, but I have found the best solution for keeping track of my most important/urgent tasks as well as those tasks I call “low hanging fruit” — those I can accomplish in a quick moment while I’m driving, waiting somewhere or quickly during a down moment. 

It’s taken some fine-tuning, but Apple Reminders works perfectly for this!!  And I love that I can mark it as done and it goes to a list of completed tasks where I can view my list off accomplishments and bask in the contentedness of a job well done and time well managed!

title: Great basics, but missing powerful features for serious use
body:
I really like Apple Reminders for its clean design and easy sync across devices. It’s great for quick to-dos, recurring bills, birthdays, and simple task lists. But once you start trying to use it for time-sensitive or productivity-heavy tasks, the limitations become frustrating.

Here are the biggest issues I’ve run into:
- Repeating reminders behave like recurring tasks. If I set an hourly repeat, checking off the task doesn’t stop the alerts: it just creates the next instance. For one-time tasks with a deadline, this makes no sense. I want nagging reminders until I complete the task, not a brand-new task every hour.
- No true “repeat notifications until done” option: Many times I want reminders to start at a certain time (e.g., 10 AM) and repeat hourly until the deadline (e.g., 5 PM). But if I mark it complete at 3 PM, it should stop there. Right now, it keeps recreating the reminder until the end date, even if I already finished the task.
- No end repeat time: You can only end repeats by date, not a specific time of day. This makes scheduling less precise.
- Rigid repeat intervals: I can only pick from Apple’s preset options (hourly, daily, weekly, etc.). Why not let users set custom intervals (e.g., every 20 minutes, every 90 minutes, every 1 hour and 42 minutes, etc.)?
- Limited integrations: I’d love to be able to attach or link emails (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, etc.) directly to reminders. That would make following up on tasks much easier.

These improvements would make Reminders dramatically more powerful:
1. Add a “Repeat Notifications” option separate from “Repeat Tasks.”
2. Allow reminders to stop repeating as soon as they’re marked complete.
3. Add end-repeat by time, not just date.
4. Allow fully customizable repeat intervals.
5. Support linking/attaching emails and other external items to reminders.

Reminders is a solid app for casual use, but with just a few updates it could rival third-party apps like Alarmed, TickTick, or  Due for better productivity. I hope Apple considers adding these features as it would transform Reminders from a “basic to-do list” into a true productivity tool.

title: My Lists  Are Not Cooperating
body:
I’m glad that Apple seems to finally be getting some women on the design team. I find it asinine that Reminders & Calendar are finally (sloppily) integrated. However, why do I lose my customization from Reminders > Lists when it goes into Calendar?                                                                                                                             Example:                                                                                  
In the Calendar - Job is 🧢 cobalt blue My School 🎓is maroon 
In the Reminders - My School 🎓 List is maroon                               
In Calendar, “Scheduled Reminders” is faintly different from cobalt blue & I cannot edit it WHY!??! Does that seem like it would cause some confusion?

Adding a particular Note to a reoccurring Reminder can’t be added at this time, so I have to delete the Reminder & recreate it. When I recreate it, it wants to be a subcategory of my main Reminder List, rather than My School 🎓 List.

A few other issues that I can not schedule with Reminders:
* Why can’t I create a Reminder that happens every 2nd Wednesday?
* Why do I need to create a separate reminder for early release days?                                                                                                  

Seriously Apple get some moms on this!

I also think that allowing Reminders to collaborate with Tasks or just removing one program altogether and renaming the app to something like “To Do Lists” would be better. title: App is like an iceberg.
body: I have a lot of different apps on my iPad for this purpose. To be honest, none of them were free, that is, they were free, but for example, only for 5 items that you want to add to the list for reminders, which is practically not practical and everyone knows that this limited number is not useful! Until I saw a video on YouTube about the secret tricks of the Apple Reminders app and without hesitation I came back to this app, which seemed so interesting at first!! But now I can boldly recommend to you that this is the freest and best app in this category. Rest assured that it is the truth. I gave it one star because a question has been bothering my mind as to why I, along with many other users, should not be aware of how many different features have been added to this app over the years and we are not aware of it. And I also have a request: if at the final stage, when we have completed our list and want to print it with a printer, I wish it were possible to display beautiful templates and different color schemes in the list design for selection on the screen. Thank you to the development team and thank you for reading.

It’s simple to set up, intuitive to use, and integrates seamlessly with iCloud for syncing across devices. I use it daily to manage work tasks and stay on top of my medication schedule. The clean interface and dependable notifications make it an essential part of my routine.

title: Good; could be a lot better
body: It’s a good app and it does the basics well.  It has some advanced features but so many seem to be needlessly limited.  For instance, when creating a smart list, there’s no reason I shouldn’t be able to use multiple different filtering criteria such as which lists (currently can only limit to one list) to pull from.  Should also be able to batch code tags as well as a function allowing us to auto code tags in standard lists based on the list and even section (shouldn’t be reserved for smart lists).  I’d also like it if I could set the time slots for the today list’s morning, afternoon and evening categories.    I do really like the calendar integration though but should be able to set a duration on a tag so it shows up appropriately.  Somewhat unrelated but should also be able to zoom more on calendar so that everything falls in line as long as it doesn’t overlap rather than things being placed side by side even when they’re at different times.   This is particularly problematic for things like reminders or calendar events lasting 15 minutes or less.

title: ADHD friendly/ simple & completely free!
body:
The only thing I find that can be modified is making the subtasks reappear without another reminder like I list my animal care routine that’s daily and house cleaning things and break them down into smaller tasks and I don’t like a thousand reminders but for them to be checked off again I have to repeat the task with a time and day and times are different at times. Sometimes they have no time but just a list of the items that reoccurs without a reminder under the main task that is scheduled and repeated would be nice! 

I have ADHD and it’s pretty friendly for having that there’s no reward or noise when checking it off like what my Finch App has but I didn’t find much dopamine boost with the extra noises and rewards from checking tasks off finch app so I said well although i have that I’m going to establish everything that’s a actual todo item in here. so didn’t really lose anything other than having multiple reminders since I can’t just have it repeat without doing a date and time which I wish they would change. Then it would be PERFECT! 
LOVE the widget that you can put a on your screen to see everything as well on any of your lists!!! Only app really I have found that option with everything else for free!! Overall this is a great simple easy app for laying out your tasks for the day, week and month. Customize your lists with different colors and icons, see your tasks for all your lists, routines, and projects, one time projects and tasks with alot of different steps whatever they are. 
Even NOTES if you need notes space can put it in without a reminder or with a reminder on your screen from taking your medication to carrying your child to a sports event to a thought in your mind and also there’s the iPhone notes app I like but personally don’t use much due to liking google keep better. Every one has different preferences. 
This allows a checklist without paying anything for it and having Apple iPhone it’s already built in. looked at other things they charge you to pay for it and google tasks doesn’t have subtasks that will repeat with a repeating parent task unless the task doesn’t repeat at all but then can’t add daily reminders to it. So WIN WIN!!

title: Excellent except for one thing
body:
This app is almost perfect. It’s easy to use and I love all the options for viewing the reminders. The one big obvious flaw is that there’s no way to add a new reminder while in the “Scheduled” view. The Scheduled view provides the best snapshot of your reminders by date, so that’s my default view. But if you want to add a new reminder, you have exit that view to select “New Reminder.” 

If you’re in the “Reminders” view under the iCloud heading, there’s a function at the bottom that allows you to add a new reminder without exiting that view. But that view doesn’t break out the reminders by date. 

DEVELOPERS: Can you add that same functionality to the bottom of the “Scheduled” view? Then the app would be a perfect five stars.

title: No offline support
body: It's indefensible to completely disallow offline reminder creation. The technology to cache changes locally and sync them when you reconnect has been around since well before iOS and the fact they can't support this basic feature is frustrating. Guess I'm back to Google Keep, which doesn't become completely useless whenever I'm not connected to the internet (i.e. in a rural area, on the subway, in a crowded space where cell towers are overloaded). I understand that Apple prioritizes a seamless experience and offline caching complicates that, but I regularly think of things when I don't have a cell signal and being unable to create reminders makes this app far less useful than it could be.

title: Some basic usability flaws
body: Quite a few basic issues that Reminders app has still puzzle me. It doesn’t know the difference between the “the morning” and “tomorrow“ in so many instances. The suggestions of times makes using the app take longer. If I need to be reminded to do something at 4 PM, I’m not going to need the reminder at 4 PM yet. Reminders wants this to be the case. The widget functionality is not so good either. And when you accidentally click a reminder as done, good luck, trying to find it in the sea of other Reminders. I’m not sure why you can’t just make a recently completed list and make it easier for us to find the Reminders, we didn’t want deleted because of usability issues in the first place.

✅ With folders, smart folders, subfolders, and tags, the organization is the best I’ve ever used.
✅ With swipe and long-press menus, the management is also the best I’ve ever used.

✅ Great icon and color options for lists.
✅ Great set of widgets available.
✅ A number of ways to be reminded (time, location, and other triggers).
✅ List templates are super useful.

BAD: I honestly can’t come up with any negative comments.

title: Love this app!
body:
I love reminders. I use it for school, and it’s a great way to structure things. I have two requests that would make the app perfect, though:
(DEVELOPERS PLEASE READ)
1. Make it more customizable. For example, give users the ability to change the app icon colors without getting another app or making it tinted black, or give the option to change the background or colors of the reminders.
2. Give users the ability to structure differently. Instead of it going into the three sections (morning afternoon and tonight) based on their exact time, let us move the reminders into those sections even if they aren’t on a time schedule. 
For example: I have to do certain tasks in the morning, but I sometimes sleep in, so I hate having it notify me when I’m not ready to do it yet. So it just yelling at me if I don’t get it done at some point in the morning would be amazing!
Anyway, the app in general is great, I just wish we had those abilities stated above. Thanks Apple, for a great built in app to help everyone out!

title: Reminders Rocks, Siri not so much
body: Whenever I’m setting a reminder, I typically use Siri to set it. When I ask Siri to set a reminder for a certain day, series is very responsive and understands. But then when I ask for the reminder to include a time in the description, the reminder is changed to be set for that time. For instance, if I say “hey Siri set a reminder for Tuesday at 6” Siri will respond with “ what do you want to be reminded about?” I will respond with something like “ call dad at seven” and the reminder will then be set for today at seven. This is very inconvenient, and also affects my ability to be reminded about the things that I need to remember.

body:
I’ve been using Reminders for… years because making lists matches how I plan. From grocery lists to larger projects, the reminders app is really useful. I think the newer features are fantastic additions, such as nested lists and sections. 

The one feature that I wish it had is the ability to add a reminder to more than one list. For example, I can buy some things at more than one store, such as light bulbs— I can find them at the grocery store or the hardware store or some other stores. I have a grocery store list and a hardware store list. It would be really nice to be able to create one entry for light bulbs and have it show up on both lists. If I happen to go to the grocery store first and pick up the light bulbs there, marking the item as complete would remove it from all lists. Some other list apps have this feature.

Point is Apple doesn’t care about their software. Going to have to recreate a list and delete the old one just to get rid of the completed items bug. How is this company the most valuable in the world is baffling.

title: Flawed Design for Repeating Tasks
body:
I use Apple Reminders to manage my daily routines, with a repeating task called “Daily Tasks” that has 10 subtasks. If I don’t mark the subtasks as done, they correctly appear the next day when the parent task repeats. But if I do mark them as done, they don’t show up the next day.

This might be “working as designed,” but it’s a flawed design. Subtasks should reset automatically with the parent task when it repeats—otherwise, it defeats the purpose of tracking daily habits.

Also, why is there no straightforward way to submit bug reports or feedback? This makes resolving issues unnecessarily frustrating. Please address this!

title: Great, but limited notification options
body:
I love several things about this app, from the collaboration tools, to nested tasks, to repeating reminders.

However, the thing that always irks me is the lack of configuration options for HOW I am reminded of various things.  There’s no per-list or per-item configuration. So either you get notified with the same sound for every task that is due, or you get notified of nothing.

I would love to be able to set a separate sound and priority per list so that when something is added to my grocery list, maybe I get a banner, but no sound, but when an important timed reminder arrives, I get a very obvious sound on my phone or watch.

I would also like to set hourly repeating reminders with a subtle sound (but longer description than allowed in the alarm/timer app)

The notification options are just frustrating if you’re trying to use this app for more than a single simple to do list.

title: Competes with paid to-do apps
body:
I recently switched back to iOS and decided to take Reminders out for spin before looking at paid apps. I’m glad I did. 

For my personal use case, this app is perfect and more than adequate for extensive, daily use tracking detailed to-dos.

With iCloud enabled, the app provides:

- tags; filtering by tag
- task categories (each category is a section in main view)
- optional date/time indication
- tasks that automatically move to the next day when not completed as scheduled
- recurrence; custom recurrence scheduling
- integration with Calendar such that the Calendar widget shows Reminder tasks alongside calendar items

title: The good, the bad, and the suggestion
body: I have used many other task management apps and I know that this is a part of the Apple ecosystem. I love the improvements made to this app and am constantly coming back to it for the ease of use. It now offers automatic grocery categories, which is really helpful. I’m still trying to figure out the best use of smart lists, but that’s a me thing. You can group lists into folders, have lists with sections, kanban views, etc…. But my personal issue is… I wish I could choose and customize the lists colors and color code the tags, much like in Apple Calendar. I also wish I could not have scheduled and assigned tasks (like in a family list but assigned to another family member) show up and clutter my personal to-do list for the day (I prefer the auto “today” list for my widget).

title: Great app! Highly recommend!
body:
I have been using this app for years now to remind me of so many different things such as appointments, special dates, when to take prescriptions, when to make a special phone call, and so many more different reminders. If I want to remember something  on a future date I enter it. It's so very easy to use.  I can delete reminders that are finished to keep it cleaned up. I can set option to repeat it regularly or as a one time reminder. I can add a note. Adding a phone number creates a link to the phone app to directly dial it. Adding new reminders is easy. Editing existing ones also easy.  I'm 74 .. At my age it is good to have a tool like this, even though my memory is still good and in tact, I use this app so I don't need to worry about forgetting important things having to do with a time line. Plus these reminders are saved automatically in my iCloud account so I won't lose the list.
Best reminder app I've ever used.

title: Great recent updates; Few suggestions for future
body:
A nice app that I use regularly. It has many good features and is not buggy. A few suggestions for Apple developers:
1. Well done incorporating reminders into iCal!! Would like the ability to hide completed reminders in that view, and even a toggle on/off reminder view in iCal iOS (where space is less) would be ideal. 
2. Would like the ability to print iCal calendar(s) with Reminders in one view, preferably separated so timed appts are separate from reminders, to see all to-do items plus appointments on one page. I would use this for daily, weekly, and even monthly views printed out. 
3. Great recent update allowing Reminders view in customizable columns!  However when i create a smart list of reminders for this week, those columns headers disappear and therefore there is no organization. Would love to be able to maintain the column headers on smart lists, plus on all is/ios devices. 
Thanks for a great app! Yet another example of a reason to be an Apple user!

body:
Scenario: A list of Upcoming reminders and a complimentary list of longer term upcoming reminders.
Result: Impossible 

There are two logical approaches.
1. Create a list with 2 different date ranges, one inclusive and one exclusive.
2. Create a list with the longer date range that also excludes the shorter range smart list.

Problem with 1, you can’t specify more than one date range.
Problem with 2, you can’t include or exclude a smart list.

Both problems are foolishly lazy programming.

title: Slipping into obsolescence
body:
I have relied on this app for years to manage a handful of recurring cyclical list such as groceries or packing for a trip. In which I will repeatedly remove items only to add them back later. For this purpose, it’s quite annoying that there is no search bar in individual lists, you can only search items in all of reminders at once. So the workflow keeping track of a large list involves constantly going back to the main page to search and see if you’ve already got an item on the list list uncheck it, and then returning to the main list. The real problem begins for me, because as of recently, I have noticed that search is not indexing all of my list anymore. In fact, it’s not indexing my most used list, my grocery list, at all. So every time I want to quickly find an uncheck a few items by name from the completed list, I have no way of searching for them in the many many items on that reminder list. And when I do finally find that item and uncheck it, if I return to search on the main page, it will then be found in the search results.

This is for the developers, please fix this bug or reconsider the logic if it is part of a misguided feature. I can only assume since some completed items do return in results there is a logic at play. Whether it is certain lists, or items created at older than a certain date that are not being shown, it is making the app that I have used for years for multiple every day tasks completely obsolete enforcing me to figure out new solutions.

title: Works OK - but could easily be MUCH better
body:
It’s a list maker, with categories and some other ways of identifying what type of To Do item each is. 

The problem is the interface, or lack there of. To put it in perspective, my ancient Palm Pilot had a better to do list. One major thing: it is very cumbersome to do something as easy as change the due date on an item, and you can’t select many and batch change the date. This is where a lot of Apple’s apps bite the dust. It is easy to tell that they don’t actually use their own apps. If they actually did, they would realize the need to quickly change the date on everything that was due yesterday, and is still on the list, to the current date. Unfortunately, to do so you have to go into the detail view of each item, pull up the calendar and select the current date. With my ancient Palm Pilot? Just a quick pull down menu on the actual to do item and a smart selection of:  Today, Tomorrow, One Week, Other. Quick, simple. Should the first three options not be exactly what is wanted, the fourth option would open a calendar and let you select a specific date. But let’s face it, those top three options would probably be selected 98% of the time. 

The importance/urgency hierarchy does NOTHING. If this were actually functioning like it should, the items that are rated as “important / urgent” = !!! Would automatically go to the top, ALWAYS - regardless of whether or not other tasks were overdue. Guess what Apple programmers? We can see that the date is red on the to do items, so we know they are overdue. They don’t all need to be sitting at the top of my list as if they were all the most critical. Like everyone else, I have items on my To Do list that are… wait for it… important / urgent that I NEED to get done and then I may list a few other items I could also possibly do that day, but are NOT important / urgent. When I use the Important/urgent selection, it just shows that there are some !!! next to it. So you have to search through your list to find them.

Ah, Apple programmers (assuming any of you actually READ any of these critiques, which you probably don’t), I know what you are going to say: “ You can just set it to manually move the items up or down in the list”. Well, my answer to that is… sometimes. More often than not, if you try to move an item (usually up) too much, the app gets confused and won’t “let in” the moved To Do and throws it back down to where it was. That’s some great GUI programming! (Obviously NOT)

And then there is the confusing addition of the ability to “Flag” a To Do. Not sure what the difference is between flagging a To Do and giving it an urgency rating. And, as you might imagine, given the above, flagging it does nothing. Just puts a flag on it, doesn’t move it up the list, or bold it, or nothin’. Oh, and you can’t change the color of the flag - so you could categorize the To Do items: Home, Work, Shopping, Pet, Something Else…

You CAN put each item in a different category / folder. Which then allows you to search through a specific category to see all the items in it. But if you don’t put a date on items in categories you won’t ever see them unless you go into these other lists. There is a descriptor at the bottom of each To Do saying what category (folder) it is in. But it is small and has no distinguishing features.

The only thing that makes this To Do list useful is what makes all of Apple’s less-than-well-done apps useful: it ties into the Apple eco-sphere so I can add a ToDo on my computer, edit it on my iPad, and then call it up again on my iPhone. Hurray! The product manager for this app actually allowed the backbone functionality of Apple’s Operating Systems to… function!

I can only assume that being the product manager or developer on this app is some kind of punishment and that the budget to work on / improve it is non-existent. 

It would be great if all the senior execs at Apple actually “ate their own dog food” - in other words used their products. I don’t doubt that all of them OWN these products, but I am sure it is their assistants that actually use them. And if I were such an assistant, I wouldn’t criticize anything either - I’m sure they like their jobs and Apple execs are known for their huge egos and less than stellar talent and I’m sure would quickly get rid of anyone who actually tried to speak truth to power. Especially when it comes to coding and apps. “Yeah, but Maps now has TREES! In 3D even!”

Apple benefitted from Steve Jobs’s guidance NOT because he was a “genius” but because he had a vision for the products HE wanted. And those products just happened to be products we wanted too. And his sensibilities for ease of use and design also were what all of us users wanted too. He was constantly reigning in the engineers from overcomplicating things or the designers (*cough* Ives *cough*) from losing site of functionality. And, while Mr. Cook is obviously a smart executive that has done many things right, he even admits that he is not a “product guy” which unfortunately leaves the inmates to run the asylum.

body:
I've been using the Apple Reminders app for years, and it has consistently met my needs. The app is user-friendly and intuitive, making it easy to create and manage tasks. One of the standout features is how Apple continually updates the app with relevant and useful features. Whether it's adding location-based reminders or integration with other Apple services, the app keeps getting better. 

I also love the ability to share reminders with family and friends, which has been incredibly helpful for coordinating tasks and events. Overall, I highly recommend the Apple Reminders app to anyone looking for reliable and versatile task management tool.

title: Useful tool for moms
body: I am a list person, if I don’t have it on a list I don’t remember to do a chore or pick up an item at the store.  My problem was, every conventional method no longer worked for me, because I have 5 children whom like to erase my dry erase list, color and draw on my paper list, or spill their water right where my list is setting. Worst of all, I usually walk around with my list and set it down somewhere and forget where I put it. This app has helped solve all these problems. I keep my phone on me at all times, the kids can’t get to my list to erase or draw on it. And if I loose it I can use our MacBook to help me find it again. I see that a chore needs to be done every time I pull out my phone and scheduling out my chores helps me to prioritize and plan my chores better. Not to mention the satisfaction of checking off an item and it disappearing when the task is complete.

title: Let me begin by saying...
body:
Ever since I was a child, I have absolutely despised farts. The pure feeling of rumbling in my stomach as my bowels fill with the gas of death strikes fear into my heart. My rectum opening up to release the foul stench of rotting flesh in the form of an atomic bomb could NOT have been less enjoyable to me.

HOWEVER, there was always a pattern to the attacks from the fart monster. They became predictable. I noticed as I aged, and became more mature. I was observant. I was smart. I was no longer the weak child I once was. I could FIGHT the wrath, had I devised a successful plan to prepare myself for the torture.

title: Very Helpful
body:
Love to schedule repeating tasks. 
Easy to make lists. 

Only downfall to me is the inability to copy a “Reminder” list and paste it into “Notes”. You can only transfer one item at a time, not the whole list, so you basically have to re-write the entire list into “Notes”. title: Works great, still room for improvement
body:
There is nothing better than raising your wrist, and saying to your Watch “Hey Siri, remind me when I get home that there are groceries in my trunk.” The Reminders app syncs reliably, and provides a really nice experience if you and your spouse share a Shopping list. Not only can you both add to food categories, but you can check things off in real time if you are both at the grocery store together, and they sync.

But there is room for improvement. The interface for changing the time and date of a to-do item is clunky. They added a button to supposedly make it easier, but it only helps if you happen to want to postpone your reminder to tomorrow or whatever fixed time they provide. When you look at an item in your list, why can’t you tap on the time/date to change it?

title: More powerful Reminders, so close…just needs a few more things…
body:
The improvements to Reminders the last year or so have made it a very capable application, similar to OmniFocus and other GTD-based products.  The folders and sections provide a good organizing approach, with tags going across them.  Integration with Siri is excellent as well as the ability to link other things.

The integration needs to be consistent, however.  Apple Mail items can only be linked from MacOS (an incredibly useful feature, but doesn’t work on iOS/iPadOS).  Apple Notes links are poorly done except on iPadOS (where a drag and drop works, but nowhere else).  Missing a link between calendar entries and reminders is a glaring omission.

Finally, better formatting support in the Notes section would allow you to generate status reports directly.  Today, the formatting doesn’t work when you print to PDF…basically a bug as it doesn’t even handle line breaks, let along italics or bold.

Clean these up across the device types and you’d have an amazing set of personal productivity apps, integrated together!

body:

title: Keep Your LIfe on Track!
body:
Love, love, love Reminders.  Wow, I can set up a notification for anything I need to be reminded to do daily, weekly, monthly, yearly and in a sequence that works best for me. 

  I use this app almost daily and it helps me to not forget anything I need to do whether it is stop by the grocery, (and the list), doctor's appt., home repair appt, events, you name it, you can save it and have your phone remind you in any format that works best for you. 

I also love that I can keep a list for replacement household items like HVAC filter size, ink printer cartridge model numbers, anything that I might need to pick up and discover, AFTER I get to the store, that I forgot to check the size or model number I need before leaving home!

My favorite part of the set up is that I can have it remind me, one day in advance, and then one hour before the event.  I haven't missed anything since I started using Reminders.

title: Why not update all iOS versions of this app?
body:
Okay, I have an older iPad and a newer phone. The phone puts my grocery list into categories for easier sorting and use among the store aisles but the version running on our older devices doesn’t. Why can’t Apple update all versions of this app running on all versions of iOS and iPadOS (also MacOS) so categories work correctly across all my devices? I thought apps on differing devices sharing data on iCloud were supposed to work exactly the same way. Evidently this yet another thing Apple does to get customers to abandon older but perfectly functional devices and shell out big bucks for a newer device. Not nice.

Update: not only has Apple NOT addressed the issues, it doesn’t even respond to let me know they even read this review. I thought Apple was supposed to be the customer centric tech company. Guess not!

title: List and Grocery Lists
body:
My family and I love this feature in IOS. We have several “Grocery” or shopping list set up. We have one for Urgent items, one for our weekly grocery shopping trip, and a few others for misc. items. Our urgent list is for something needed the same day, like milk, eggs, or bread.   In addition to our grocery and urgent grocery lists, I have a Home Depot List, and a Walmart list. We get out trash bags, dish soap, and a few other bulk items at HD and a lot of HBA products at Walmart. 

I have shared and allowed editing to all family members. This allows them to check off purchased items or modify an item. For example, I may put paper towels on grocery list.  My wife might go in and add or edit “paper-towels” adding, select a size, Bounty.  I have my list with Headings for each isle of our grocery store. This keeps me in direct isle to isle travel pattern and prevents going back and forth grabbing things I forgot.  The headings I use are tailored for my specific stores product locations.  For example: Produce, Deli, Breads, Meats, Soups & Condiments, Cookies, Crackers, & Snacks, Frozen Foods, Paper Products, Cereal, Paper Products, Animal Feed, Soda & Waters, Milk & Dairy. Your lists organization or Headings orders and or names maybe different.  No two stores are set up in exact same manner.  

The only drawbacks I have found, have nothing to do with app, but the user/s. I highly recommend adding and sharing the whole family to the list. Make sure to allow editing for all members. If multiple people do the shopping, you must ensure whoever does the shopping marks purchased items off the list. One other suggestion is, if you have a picky person and or eater in the home, make them be specific in their entries. Example, my daughter loves Goldfish, original, cheddar, baked only. If I come home with extra cheddar or something different she will not eat them.  Example #2, my wife will add baggies to the list. Anyone who shops knows there are 12+ sizes and types of baggies. From snack to gallon and larger sizes, then you need to know storage or freezer, this is where the notes section comes in handy. Use it. You won’t be disappointed (this agin reflects back to the beginning of my review where I recommend allowing all members to edit the list). 

You may have to make some tweaks or modifications for your local store but once done it’s good to go for every shopping trip.  

In all it’s a great app or feature for the IPhone. Our family uses it daily.  Siri helps when we are feeling lazy too, just say, “Siri add Milk to Grocery List 1”, and voila, it’s done! I use this app for business as well but that’s a whole other review.  I recommend this app to any family that is on the move with hectic schedules.
 
Hope this helps,
BSC
Katy, TX

title: Needs Better Notification Options
body:
I use Reminders, because that’s the option that I have as an iPhone user. However, it really needs the option to “remind” me to do stuff. Notifications that aggressively say, “HEY, MORON! DO THIS IMPORTANT THING THAT YOU WANTED TO REMIND YOURSELF THAT SUPPOSED TO DO!”

As someone who grew up racing motorcycles at a time when helmets were something that you put on if you happened to think about it, I’ve got a LOT of memory issues related to past concussions. 

I can literally realize the need to do something, write that something down, then walk out the door to do it and forget why I left the house. Not kidding. 

The iCal app constantly throws banners up on my phone screen to remind me about stupid holidays for social media “friends” that I’ve never actually met in person and religious holidays for religions I’ve never heard of, but I consider myself lucky if the “Reminders” app gives me a single hint. How about a tap on the wrist from my watch, banners on my screen and maybe some noise to let me know that I need to do something that I’ve marked as important? 

I don’t claim to know much when it comes to technology. I love gadgets and tech, but I grew up during a time when that stuff was made in Japan and instructions were so confusing that we just figured stuff out. We didn’t have YouTube videos or online detailed user manuals … heck, we blew into our Atari cartridges to get them to work, (and that actually made a difference, even though they claim to this day that it didn’t!)

 But what I do know is that I want things to work a certain way and regardless of the many Notification Settings in REMINDERS, I’m telling you, it’s not as aggressive as iCal about reminding me of stuff. It needs to do better. 

The Geo Notification option is cool, but again, how about opening the app to that particular list when I arrive at the store’s address? How about the option to bump my watch and put a huge thing on my screen when a specific time reminder comes due? How about kicking me in the nads or hitting me over the head with a cooking pot when I’m supposed to call someone or go to a certain place? Anything more aggressive than the timid little banner that I’m getting would be lovely. 

Maybe it does all of this and I need to look at the settings more closely or something, but it feels like it’s weak in this department. I can’t figure out how to get iCal to stop telling me that it’s the birthday of a phishing social media troll whose friend request I accidentally accepted because they were mutual friends with someone who I thought screened friends better, or that it’s the Founder’s Day of an elusive tribe of Aborigine headhunters half a world away, but for some reason, I don’t notice the reminder that I’m supposed to stop and pay my electric bill while I’m in town, because that was in the Reminders App instead of my iCal. (Also, the two should communicate and share stuff - if I put something into Reminders, it’d be great if that also appeared in my iCal so I could go back and easily see what day I did something. Maybe I’m the only one who wants such a feature, I don’t know). 

Other than that, it’s a really cool app and has sooooo much potential — if it would just do a better job of that one thing that the name suggests … actually remind me, I’d give the darn thing 5 stars instead of three! 

Again, maybe my own ignorance of how to properly use it, but if I can figure out how to properly use all of my other apps, then maybe this one needs to be easier for dummies like me to figure out? Just saying. 😉

title: Synchronization with Calendar, Please!
body:
Reminders has come a long way and it has earned a solid three stars from me after adding support for auto-sorting grocery lists. This single feature has changed the way grocery shopping works in our family for the better!

To earn the final two stars from me, I would love to see synchronization between Reminders and Calendar across the Apple ecosystem. I plan my days out in Reminders and then I have to manually convert these tasks to calendar events. It would be amazing if there a way to automate this process somehow. Maybe look to apps like Fantastical to see how they achieve this process?

title: Why is this app slowing down?!
body:
Even just a month ago, I would have given this app five stars.  That’s not the case today. 

I like to keep busy, and I take my personal resolutions _deadly seriously,_ so I appreciate having an app on my phone (that is seldom more than a couple of feet away at a given time) to help remind me to check my plants on a given day or take medication at a certain time or even remind me of simple commitments (walking 10,000 steps every day and no more reading US comics published in 1992 or beyond!) , because when I get engrossed in something, I may forget myself. 

Now, when I tick off certain goals on this app, it takes up to thirty seconds for the thing to confirm—or worse, it doesn’t confirm, and I’m not certain if that checkbox is actually checked!

Yes, I rebooted the device. 

So, am I going to have to find a third-party solution, when the one already built into my phone is on the fritz?  And what does that say about Apple product?

title: Just an app I hadn’t used until suddenly it changed my life!
body:
I don’t know how many years this app has been on my phone and I never bothered to open it. I’d been using iCal or the Calendar App for ever—but it refused to sync between my phone and my iPad. I forgot to check it. I forgot to add new things. The Calendar app is cumbersome. It’s easy to spend ten minutes adding information and then accidentally close the window and it doesn’t save the date!

One day I opened Reminders instead, wondering if it had an alarm function. Everything changed for me! It was far easier to set up dates and appointments in. More flexible. Easier to access. I had it on QuickDraw and soon I was way more organized!

Less clutter and more practical. I love it. It does exactly what I’ve always needed an app to do.

title: Satisfactory but spare
body: Apple Reminders is a workable, simple, and reliable task list. My middling rating comes from my perspective that calendar events and tasks share a kinship (even down to .ics code) and should (and can in the cal app I use) be integrated into a standard view. Apple Calendar doesn’t do this natively, and it should—one star gone. I still use it as my primary task list because I so integrate them in BusyCal or Fantastical. But—second star gone—it falls so far behind other similar apps in features. I particularly wish it had the ability to nest or create sub-tasks to a ‘project’ task. Apple made a lukewarm attempt at this but it works only within single lists and notably, does not work in the “Today” view where I (and I presume many people) live on a daily basis. It really shouldn’t be hard for Apple to get five stars in this by introducing a few more tweaks. The good news is that I’m hopeful. I see updates being made after years of dormancy.

title: Constantly skips weekly and monthly reoccurring reminders
body:
Around 4 months ago I noticed my reminders app was completely skipping reoccurring reminders, as if I had accidentally “double clicked” a reminder complete - i.e. I take a weekly medication that greatly improves the quality of my life, and 3 times now this app has marked that I have taken the medication on the day I actually took it, as well as the next week. For example, if I were to take the medication February 1st, I would mark the reminder as complete on that day, and then the app should be set up to remind me on February 7th to take my medication again. But the app will have the next reminder set on the 14th instead of the 7th, like I clicked complete twice when I know that I did not. 

I have now missed car payments, missed medications, and have missed giving my dog her monthly heart worm prevention.

Also, I realize the reminders I have that are daily I go back to the category. Those individual reminders are deleted as I mentioned they are their schedule daily to occur and there is no end date. However every time the Reminder app is deleting them and I constantly have to put them back. I’ve been using this app for years, so it’s not like I don’t know what I’m doing . Apple needs to do better I like having a to do list reminders, etc. but is an inconvenience that is constantly deleting reoccurring categories and to do list. this been going on for months and I’m so so tired of it. I’m so ready to spend extra money on a app that we get the job done. but like I said, if anyone was thinking about adding the Reminders app, please look at all the reviews since the update it has tremendously slowed and deleting recurring daily categories, and to do list which shouldn’t happen. i’ll put this as one star because is an inconvenience, especially with someone that loves to have a to do list in reminders to get things done.

title: Glad I made the switch!
body:
I have tried many task apps, some paid, some free, and ignored Reminders because it was too basic. After seeing the capabilities expand I finally switched, and am so happy I did - it’s much easier to use with Siri and Share than third party apps, and I love the way they create visual previews when you save links. The shortcut feature I liked so much from todoist to be able to type a due date and time was a big one for me too, it’s not quite as seamless but close enough. Notifications functionality also better - I love the snooze option!

Knocked off a star because the subtasks feature is way too basic, and seeing subtasks on Mac is nearly impossible.  Would be great to have a carrot expand inline to see subs in your list, or at the very least have them show by default in the task without having to scroll, find and open separately.

body:

I love this app but unless this is fixed I’ll need to use another option.

title: Could be much better.
body:
19 Jan 2024

Of course Tasks have been in constant use since the first iPad and there have been many tweaks and improvements along the way; but, the one thing that is drastically needed is to look at apps like Fantastical which integrate tasks and calendars together for a single point of entry as well as a single view.  Until this is done, I cannot add teo more stars to the rating.  I also thing the UX using the Task App is flawed with too many steps to add subtasks, and additional info in a task (notes, urls, etc.) and it does not have a way to define dependencies like, ‘y cannot be done until x has been completed’.  Not looking for a full fledged project planner; but, even as a minimum, we know some tasks are dependent on another.

I really think Apple really needs to sit down at the design table and look at combining calendar and task apps together.

title: Useful, although some improvements could help
body:
I have switched to keeping my to-do list, groceries list, and even date night idea list on this app. Some tools are helpful such as being able to share specific lists with others. 

The “project management” features could still use some improvement. For example, assigning a task to someone else doesn’t appear to work very well, or at least it doesn’t show the task as being assigned to them until you click to edit the details of the task. Not practical if you’re trying to see at a quick glance who has been assigned what. 

Also, when categorizing the shopping list, items will “auto-sort” into the subcategories the app has set by default (deli, veggies, snacks, etc) but when someone else who you have shared the list with tries to do it, it either doesn’t sort them, or created duplicate subcategories, or doesn’t sync properly with the others on the list.

The “smart lists” feature is incredibly confusing. I think it either needs a new name so it isn’t so misleading as to its use case, or it needs to be completely overhauled. I’ve looked up several discussions online where people share a similar sentiment. 

The app should probably decide between being a simple “to-do list” app or a “project management” tool. I don’t think doing a poor job at both is doing anyone any favors

title: I remind myself about movies and books
body:
This application is extremely useful!  If I add a movie to my Movies To See list, e.g., I can include little notes under the title, indicating genre or whether the movie is a remake or based on a book.  I can date the movie based on its release date, whether it was released in the past or hasn’t yet been released, and see my movies listed chronologically or alphabetically.  I can even create tags, so I can see just of the Puppet Master films or just Star Wars films listed in order of release date.  And, once I watch a movie, I can set the item as completed—that way, if I ever cannot remember whether I’ve seen some particular movie, it’ll tell me.

Everything I can do with my movies list, I can also do with books I want to read, or meals I want to try at different restaurants, or anything else.

title: It Does All The Things
body:
Some negative reviewers have not looked at the choices in the app menu. Such as, notifications are alarmed or silent. You can get reminded hourly if you set a time to be reminded. You can have lists within lists… for every day if you want… use section headings.
And all those sections can be side-by-side, or in a vertical list. 
AND THERE IS SO MUCH MORE. 
Apple’s native Reminders app is easy to learn, simple to use, yet it is super-feature-rich. 
And it’s free. 
Reminders has replaced all the other task apps I have tried and deleted. 
This one is “it” for me.

title: Great App EXCEPT
body:
PROS: I love that I can set up tasks for in the future with early reminders. I really like that I can set up custom repeats like weekly on Mondays and Thursdays. I like that I can have several different lists. I like that I can add notes. 
CONS: I generally look at the app in the morning so when I see something that I completed the previous day I want to show it as completed that day, not today since it may be a daily repeat and then there’s not an opportunity to show today’s completion. A solution to this could be that the app makes me go through extra steps to show that I want the completion date to be a date other than today. Occasionally when I select several items and reset the due date as today or tomorrow, the repeat is removed and this is very inconvenient because it may be a week or month before I realize that the task is gone and I have to rebuild it. The priority symbol just takes up space and makes it harder to see the actual task title. Subtasks seem like a great feature but I haven’t found a good way to make them work for me although I’ll keep trying.

title: I can’t live without, but lacks some basics
body: I’ve been using Reminders for years to keep me organized. It has been a lifesaver in a lot of ways! I’ve been happy with the improvements that the developers have made over the years, however, some of the basic logic in the filtering is still not all that great. Recently I’ve been watching a lot of youtube videos on how to use Reminders in conjunction with Calendar and the other productivity tools and while I feel apple is getting there in fixing some of its work flow and productivity tools, it looks like that apple assumes everyone’s work flow is the same! One thing that bugs me with the smart lists is that the date “relative range” logic isn’t intuitive. For example, I made a smart list that shows me tomorrow’s reminders, but it actually shows me today’s reminders AND tomorrow’s! I get that parts of “today” fall in the “Next 1 day” relative range, but when you are trying plan each day not based off a hourly range this makes no sense for time blocking. Also, it should be more intuitive how to link calendar events with reminders, and events or remind shouldn’t always default to alert you with a notification. I get enough pop-ups on my screen already when it comes to messages and other apps that I find this absolutely distracting. Reminders appeal is that it is built in to apple’s devices and as an apple user you can seamlessly move from one device to the next without interruption, but if this is the case apple should understand that its built in workflow tools need to be extremely robust rather than just an after thought.

title: I am a heavy user
body:
I use reminders to plan all roles of my life from daily work, to weekday and weekend tasks, to life’s financial planning goals, a total of 
I use iPhone, iPad, Mac mini and MacBook Air. 
I am constantly moving tasks from life’s role list to weekday or weekend lists, and then moving them up and down the lists to prioritize my day. I and modifying tasks dozens of times every day. 
I can’t move tasks between lists on Macs. And I can’t move them up or down the list for priority on the 2 Mac either. That greatly reduces the usefulness of the app on those devices. 
Then on the iPhone and iPad when editing a single task item, it constantly brings up a list of over a dozen actions I can take on that task, but not a single one of those actions is useful to me.  And I can’t turn that feature off. 
I am constantly switching from one Apple device to another to complete actions on my tasks.
All that being said, the app does prioritize my hours, days and yearly goals well enough to keep using it.
I just wish it were easier.

title: Great features + poor Siri. Please add Calendar Sync
body:
With some of the latest updates Apple started including around iOS16, I’ve completed switched back to Apple Reminders. So many paid features included in competitor apps are included for free here. 

That being said, Siri needs some work. It’s hit or miss using Siri to add reminders and items to my Groceries reminder list. Too many times I’ve used Siri on my HomePod to add individual items to my “Groceries List” and forget that Siri doesn’t understand context yet. For example, I’ll say, “Hey Siri, add Oranges to my Groceries List.” and then a minute later, I’ll say something like, “Hey Siri, add Hot Chocolate as well.” only to find that she added some random song from Apple Music titled Hot Chocolate to my music library.

Another example was when I try adding certain items like “banana bread” Siri thinks I’m calling out individual items and proceeds to add Bananas and Bread to my Groceries List.

It’s not every time something weird like this happens, but it’s often enough to start making me want to stop using Siri and just grab my phone to add items manually. 

Lastly, please please consider syncing Reminders to my Apple Calendar. I would really love being able to pull up my Calendar to review my day seeing all events and reminders in one place.

title: It does so much in a simple to use way.
body:
Could the app be more visually appealing? Sure.
Would that make a difference on how simply functional the app is? No.

The app makes adding new items easy and pretty intuitive. You can share a reminder list with other folks. Which is great for grocery lists. (Yes, I had forgotten the paper ones at home more than once.)
If yoy want someone to buy a specific product, you can take a picture and add it to the reminder and the other person can easily view it. You can also rearrange items easily which is great groceries if you know the lay out of the store.

When you have finished the item, it is easy to remove it, but if you remove an item by accident, it is pretty easy to find it and re-add it. It would be great if it would sort the "done" item with most recent on top. (It did that for a while.) Alphabetical is great, but sometimes I am not sure what my chunky fingers deleted by accident. 

The only thing that I would like to see come back/ be added, is a better recognition of an imported list of items. My wife likes to email me a list of ingredients for something, and I USED to be able to add it to a reminder list and hit enter and the program would separate the items in to individual reminders. This function doesn't seem to be working any more. So now I have to manually enter each item. Most of the time not that big of a deal. However at Thanksgiving and Christmas it can take half an hour or more to individually enter each item.

title: Avid User - could be improved
body:
First of all, I use this thing every dang day of my life.   If I’m out running errands, I don’t have to remember when I get home to ask my husband about something I just saw or send an email to the school about something my daughter decided to tell me we need for school tomorrow.  I just use Siri to set a reminder.  
If I need to follow up with someone next Friday to make sure something got done, I set a reminder.  
If I need to remember when I get where I’m going to add something to my shopping list, I just set a reminder to tell me when I get there.  
If I have a meeting after work hours, I set a reminder to let me know (because I’ve already walked away from my computer). 
However, there are some drawbacks:
You MUST specify a date and time (two different fields) or the reminder will not pop up on your screen. It just stays in the app, totally useless.  
The default view is what is due TODAY.  I want to see everything, in chronological order.  (Or at least have the option) But in order to view everything in chronological order, I have to make a bunch of button clicks and when I’m using this every day, all day long, I don’t want the hassle.  
Finally, this is tied to the cloud for some reason. So if I want to keep my iCloud usage low, I can’t turn off this app because all my stuff will disappear.  

I will obviously continue using this app but I also have gripes about it.

title: Transforming My Life
body:
As a long-time Apple consumer, I can't help but sing praises for the integrated Reminders app. It's a true productivity powerhouse that has transformed the way I manage my tasks and stay organized. The seamless integration across all my Apple devices ensures I never miss a beat, whether I'm on my iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

The app's simplicity is its strength. It's incredibly easy to create, edit, and prioritize tasks, making it a breeze to keep track of my to-do list. The ability to set due dates, reminders, and even location-based alerts is a game-changer, ensuring I never forget important tasks or errands.

One of the standout features for me is the natural language input. I can simply type or dictate tasks in everyday language, and Reminders intelligently understands and schedules them accordingly. This saves me precious time and makes adding new tasks a breeze.

The integration with Siri is the cherry on top. I can effortlessly add tasks using voice commands, making it a hands-free way to stay organized. Plus, Siri's proactive suggestions based on my habits are incredibly helpful.

With shared lists, I can collaborate seamlessly with family, friends, or colleagues, ensuring everyone stays on the same page. And the addition of attachments and notes to tasks adds depth and context, making it even more versatile.

In a world filled with task management apps, Apple's Reminders stands out for its elegant simplicity, seamless integration, and the sheer depth of productivity it brings to my life. It's a must-have tool for any Apple enthusiast looking to stay organized and productive.

title: Single, major flaw
body:
I like the app, especially adding items directly from the icon, but there a single, crazy deal breaker: new items are sent to the bottom of the list, and there’s no way to override(fix) it. I have lists of 40 items. When I add a new item, it is NEVER intended to be “41”. It would be much better if the newest item were up top and could be manually placed as needed. The final place for a new item is much more likely “toward the top“ then “at the very bottom“.  Instead I’ve gotta open the list drag the thing - almost always TO THE TOP!  

Minimally, there should be an setting that allows me to choose the behavior, as in “AnyList“.  I bet 90% of folks would choose “top”.  Major miss on Apple’s part, IMO.

So I’ve finally started doing that on a regular basis thanks to this app. It has been a game changer for me and my Aunt is so happy 😂. I had been making lists on occasion using the Notes app. However with iOS 17 and MacOS Sonoma I have the ability to add widgets to my Home Screen on my iPhone and on the desktop of my MacBook Pro. So now when I open my iPhone or my MacBook Pro up there is the Reminder widget staring right at me. It’s definitely helping me to stay on top of things and not to forget the little things that I did in the past. I would highly recommend it to anyone using an iPhone or a Mac.

title: The definition of “passable”
body:
I mean, this is the Reminders app. If you have an Apple product with any sort of processor inside, you own the Reminders app. If you don’t like it, there are others that can improve upon certain features. 

Any complaints feel like an old man yelling at clouds. Apple probably has a 10-year update timeline for this app and nothing I or anyone else writes in this review box will change that. 

The Siri integration is improving. The categories are improving. But it feels like you might as well invest in the GoodTasks app if you are someone like me with a LOT of things to remember. 

Apple is far ahead of the pack in many aspects of their software and firmware interfacing. Their reminders app is not a reason to buy an iPhone, but over the years it has become serviceable. 

All I want is to be able to, with a single touch on my iPhone or Apple Watch, speak a thought or reminder and have it be saved for later organization. So far Drafts is the only thing that got close to that next to Braintoss, but neither of those were granted access into the elite club of apps that have the ability to sync and edit your iOS reminders. Just add in a function like Braintoss and there you have it, every millennial/gen-z human with ADD or ADHD will forever be an Apple Stan. 

Also it’s weird how it integrates with calendars. I want to put reminders on my calendar without turning them into events. 

There are other comments/suggestions I have, but again, old man yelling at clouds. Hope that some of these features were included in the 400-year weekly update blueprint left in Steve Jobs’ last will and testament. 

I mean, if they never improve on Reminders, so what? I’ll be frustrated but it’s not like I’m buying an android any time soon. I will feed from the trough that late-stage capitalist technocrats have shoved my face into like a good boy.

title: Nope
body:
This is the dumbest app.  I can set a reminder to happen once- and that’s easy to overlook if I happen to not be near my phone at the moment and am not in the habit of looking at my notification log thing.  There’s not an alarm, just a little ding or whatever like a text.

But the biggest issue is that things don’t repeat.  You can set it to repeat every day or whatever, but it doesn’t, actually.  The internet tells you that if you mark the task complete for today, that tomorrow it’ll show up- but it doesn’t.  The reason I set a daily reminder is that I forget to do daily tasks.  Am I going to remember to recreate a reminder every day?  Um, nope.

It’s much better to use your calendar or alexa to remind you to do things- or better yet, set a reminder in your calendar and then use alexa to announce the reminder to the house, and then have the reminder banner stay on your phone until you dismiss it.  Not only have I gotten my family where they need to be on time because everyone hears the warning, but I’ve also been remembering to take my pills.

You’d think a system like apple which pretends to care so much about our health that it has a hundred ways to let them know what’s going on with your body would also want you to remember your pills.  But apparently not.  Good thing I never count on just one way to remember important things!

The reminder app is a fail.  Literally anything else is better and safer.
