title: Missing a few key QoL features
body:
The app is fine, especially considering it’s the free default task app on iOS devices. The more recent updates did add a bunch of sorely needed features, but the app isn’t quite there yet. 

First, on the Today and Scheduled list view, sub tasks need to be viewable and need to be able to be completed directly from those views. Right now, you can only see the parent Reminder and you have to go to the list that the reminder exists in to toggle sub task completion.

Second, there should be some sort of calendar-reminder integration so we can also see a glimpse of our calendar events directly in Reminders, or we should be able to see our Reminders scheduled for the day within the Calendar app. Having this be a toggleable feature in one of the apps would be nice, or having a setting within each Reminder to toggle “Show in Calendar” so that the Reminder can be viewed directly in the Calendar app, especially for repeating or task-related reminders.

title: I hate this app!
body: This app is miserable. Ive used it for a year or few dealing with this crap. This is the worst reminders app I've ever gotten! After i switched from Samsung to  apple, this was the only reminders app i could find! I struggle with memory issues and daily motivation so i have to have a reminder app to tell me to drink water, make my bed, eat food, brush my teeth, or just other things I need to do in daily life. This app is difficult to use, and extremely hard to understand!! You cannot set reminders for repeating of time, (every hour or 30 mins) I need a reminder to repeat every so often so I can remember to drink water as sometimes I go days with no water from forgetting. The thing I have a problem with most with this app though is the difficulty of understanding how it works and how to set up reminders. Nothing is explained in the app which makes this extremely difficult, when I first got this app it took me ages to find out how to even set a reminder! I would prefer if you make an app for reminders you make it easier for someone to understand. Especially a reminder app if you know people with serious memory issues are using it!!! Every time I enter the app I am confused how to set reminders and will have to look it up on Youtube. It would be appreciated if you included a help button that explains what all the buttons do, how to make folders, and how to set reminders! Every time I open the app i get confused and I cant remember how to do anything! One thing I do like is when a notification pops up with a reminder it shows every hour and you have to go into the app to mark it off. That’s very nice for my serious memory issues! If you’re reading this review as someone with memory issues of any degree, I do NOT recommend this app! Please find a different one, its just frustrating and too confusing! - Thank you for reading.

title: Like all things Apple, they ruined a good thing
body:
Ever since Steve Jobs died, it's been downhill ever since. The "reminder" app, believe it or not, once reminded you of this and that; now, however, it stops asking you when you would like to be reminded and should you forget to mention it and one long string before your cut off, it asserts that it will remind you… But it won't.

Example of how it used to work: "remind me to take out the trash," to which this Siri – like Voice would reply, "when would you like me to remind you?" You then state a date and time and voilà… Like magic.

Now, however, that same exchange goes something like this: "remind me to take out the trash,"to which the Siri like voice will reply, "okay. Added."

Headed to work, I do not know… But I know it's not added to my reminders to trigger at a sad day and time, because now, in the absence of mentioning a date and time before you get cut off, it's just as it to the growing list of reminders about which you will never be reminded. It really is disgusting.

title: It’s ok, but so close to great
body:
A bit frustrating how close this app is to being really great considering Apple’s resources. There’s just one too many thoughtless design choices for my taste. I love simplicity (why I use Things 3 instead), but Reminders is just a bit too simple for not being smart enough. 

Pros:
Free
Supports repeating tasks
Great Apple integrations (remind at location, when messaging a person)
Sub tasks, notes
List groups
Smart lists
Today list subdivides into morning, afternoon, evening

Cons:
Can’t group smart lists or shared lists (why??)
No sections to subdivide lists
Can’t choose to hide task metadata (if 2 tasks have tags, notes, reminder location, they take up the entire screen with no way to hide it)
Every option seems to be hidden behind a menu, and it isn’t very intuitive. I notice myself tapping, searching for an option, then going back because it wasn’t there so much more than in Things
Repeating tasks only able to repeat after a time period, not after completion, leading to multiple copies

Overall, a great choice if you just need simple reminders in your day to day life. Not quite smart enough to handle much more than that, though. I pretty much only use it for what Things 3 currently can’t do: location/messaging a person reminders and shared lists

title: Some improvements, some regression
body: The reminders app has received an awesome facelift and more functionality in many areas. I do not like the way that it starts making a new task just by clicking or tapping on empty space. Clicking on empty space and even hitting enter are both ways that people exit a task/text area they are already in. It results in starting tasks you didn't mean to start and having to delete them. Clicking on empty space or hitting enter should allow us to exit and finish making the task we are already in and then if I want to start typing up a new task I can hit enter or click/touch empty space again or hit the new reminder button. It also still lacks the ability to create projects. Projects are made up of tasks that you can complete to finish the main project you are working on. You can indent tasks to make them subtasks but when you see the subtask on your today view you can't see what main task it is tied to, which is important information that I then have to go digging for. The ability to set set reminders for tasks when you want to complete them is important but if you want to work on something before it is actually due or before a deadline then you don't have a way of keeping the task visible to remind you on your Today view. Sure you can set a repeating reminder until an end date but it's not the same thing since that conveys a sense of you having to do a certain task every day. For example, lets say it is Tuesday and I have a paper due next Monday, I set the due date for Monday but i clearly want to get it done before Monday, so I want to be reminded for it beforehand. Let's say I want to work on it a few days before Monday. A repeating reminder works but isn't ideal because you would get a reminder every day to work on the paper, and if you don't work on it then it appears as overdue the next day but it's not necessarily everyday that you want to work on it, but you need to know that it's there before the due date. This can be applied to wanting to get a gift for someone and the deadline is Friday but i should probably get that done a few days before or else I risk missing the date is something wrong happen. Setting a repeating reminder every day until the due date makes no sense here since I only need to complete the task once before it is fully complete, eliminating the necessity for repeating takes, I just need the task to appear on the Today group before it's due, not get alerts every day about it. Setting when or intent dates and deadline or due dates are important distinctions that should be available in a future update. In conclusion, setting projects and intention/deadline dates would be practical and effective ways of improving the workflow any Reminders users. Thank you.

title: Every new update makes it worse
body:
I use this for a very basic variety of reasons, for as long as I’ve had an iphone, and rarely add or change the tasks I have on here. But every update it changes and makes it less functional, and moves my reminders around for me and constantly adds new categories/lists that I didn’t have before and tons of extra steps. 
Like how I used to be able to check off a reminder on my Lock Screen by tapping on the banner once and marking it complete, but not only can I not complete it by the Lock Screen anymore, I have to meticulously swipe or hold down on it to them select options and THEN find the few remaining options left to use without accidentally removing the reminder from my notifications. I know most of that is down to Apple updates to the notification center that I strongly dislike, but most of the functionality I got out of this app was in the notifications and banners and now most of its function is inside the app now and I have to go through so many steps to SEE and interact with my reminders now. 
Aside from that, inside the app itself the look and location of lists and other options is really bad now and feels like someone slowly swapped out the reminders app for a totally different, lesser app, and slapped my things into lists for me. Even when I get fed up and open the app to check off my reminders it barely lets me do that, it closes me out of a list I was in last time and then when I open it again and check off the bubbles it stutters and hesitated before it jiggles around and goes away. 

I’m a comfort creature, I don’t want things to change, mainly without my input or choice, and as a person with adhd who greatly benefits from a reminder I can personalize this frustrates me that what was helpful and working for me years ago started changing and removing features and options to the point I no longer use it. 
The fact that I like having familiar things and be able to choose when and how things change is the only reason I haven’t uninstalled and searched for a new reminder app. It’s just the familiar cluster of old daily reminders I never look at and can’t see in my notifications now, and i dislike and don’t use everything to do with this now.

title: Completed items aren’t searchable
body:
In the new iOS 16 update, completed reminders are not included in search results. This is really bad! If you use reminders for shopping lists, you want to be able to quickly find common items to add to your list by just “uncompleting” them. Why not just add the item anew? 1. Item buildup. 2. Many items are complex, include a photo, metadata like availability or usage in a recipe, and it’s impractical to reconstruct this information every time. 3. Item may be in a sublist; say, as part of a recipe that you want to keep conveniently together. (In this vein, it would be useful to have a sublist item be able to appear in another list; e.g., a recipe ingredient in a Grocery Shopping list, and its recipe in a Recipes list. 
My current workaround at home is to use my non-upgraded iMac or iPad to update my list, but hopefully this will be unnecessary soon!

title: No hourly reminders?
body: **UPDATE — drag & drop gui for rearranging/recategorizing reminders is very nice 👌🏻 END UPDATE** Found reference in articles online as recent as April 2022 to an option for hourly recurring reminders but cannot find it myself in the app as of this review. This would be great to have, am currently figuring on what the best way to accomplish this will be & it’s a bummer that I’ll probably need to find some additional app to use. I wouldn’t limit such feature to hourly (as in every 1 hour) either, no reason # of hours shouldn’t be user selectable in the same way # of days is, unless there is some performance/overhead consideration. Reminders app is very useful & nicely designed overall, it does everything needed except more-frequently-than-daily reminders with minimal if any pain points in the interface. It’s an app that I use every day & helps a lot with overall organization if I make the effort to notate things consistently as they come up. I like it for keeping track of long term recurring subscription, free trial period end dates, bills that aren’t on autopay, miscellaneous tasks throughout the day that are easy to put off and forget, and so on. A shortcut to bring up the time selector directly for today reminders would be an appreciated addition 👍🏻 it’s something I do fairly often for those same-day forgetmenots & would be nice to reduce the number of taps needed to do it.

title: So slow that UI elements can get frozen on-screen on top of the Home Screen
body:
This app has precisely one redeeming feature: the fact that you can (sometimes) create a reminder by saying “Hey Siri, remind me to …”

But this advantage only exists due to Apple’s monopoly power over the iOS software platform.

And I say “sometimes” because in the last couple of years it has become so slow that now it mostly times-out and tells me it can’t do that right now.

Another thing it used to do much better is read back to me what it had transcribed.  This was infinitely valuable in the car where I could immediately ask it to make another reminder if it made a garbled Martian transcription.  (And then I could make a 3rd attempt using really simple words and simply referring to her as “my daughter” because it still can’t correctly transcribe her 2-syllable name despite her being in my contacts and one of the top-3 people I communicate with and about.)

Syncing between devices (both iOS and macOS) works about as well as interspecies limb transplantation.

The online iCloud version is such a joke that it doesn’t even let you re-order items.

I have another half-dozen complaints of equal severity.

But they still have that crucial monopoly over “Hey Siri, remind me to …”

p.s. I am a software engineer with over 30 years experience and a Master’s degree in Computer Science.

p.p.s.  I used to work on this kind of synchronization software at a big company I’m sure you’ve heard of.

title: App sometimes deletes recurring reminders
body:
I use the reminders app for one thing - to remind myself to take my daily, time sensitive, birth control pills. To do this, I set up a daily recurring reminder in the app. I’ll take my pill, “complete” the reminder, and the app creates a new one for the next day. 

Once every few months, I notice that the reminder has disappeared! This is really bad for me, because it will usually lead to me forgetting a pill and causing my period to come early. When I check the list of deleted reminders, it’s always the same problem - the app has somehow removed the setting for that reminders to recur daily, meaning that when I “complete” the reminder, it will no longer create a new one for the next day. 

Daily reminders feels like table stakes functionality for a reminders app. Even if the problem is something I’m doing as a consumer, something’s really not working with the design if it’s so easy for me to keep unknowingly making this critical mistake.

title: Suggestions from ADHD folks!
body:
So I give 4 stars because this app should work for most people but I have a small suggestion for us folks with ADHD. 
In notifications I get so accustomed to the sound of each reminder, alarm, all notifications that I subconsciously dismiss before even reading what has popped up on my screen. 
This has become a huge problem for me with my ADHD and I know what would keep me from subconsciously dismissing my reminders… if I could choose a “sound” labeled “random” and select as many sounds in a “random alert list” as I choose then I would stop assuming what my notification is. 
I have made list after list of reminders in different categories to help me read them when they pop up, and then not long after have deleted entire list because of their infectiveness. Please hear me out before you dismiss this comment. I am taking adhd medication that DOES work for me and have incorporated daily practices to help me avoid these issues but they don’t work with notifications on my phone. 

Please Apple if you are reading this, I beg you to consider! Even in alarms and calendar! 

I have many app notifications turned off to avoid distractions which means the notifications that I do get are limited to a handful of apps. A random sound for notifications will long-term be a great help for me and I believe I can speak for many specifically with ADHD and others. 

Apple, if you make this a thing, my daily life will slowly become more efficient and less sloppy. I beg you to consider this-
—from a worn out woman with ADHD to a company who’s products serve “all”!

title: Used to be a great app
body:
This used to be a practical and useful app. Now it is very clunky. None of the recent changes are improvements. 

Then: reminders would pop up on the lock screen, reminding you exactly what you needed to know. 
Now: reminders pop up, telling you that you have a time sensitive reminder, the actual reminder is not very prominent. If it’s not a time sensitive reminder, it disappears as soon as you unlock. 

Then: you could delay the reminder directly from the lock screen for an hour, later in the day, until tomorrow. Very useful!
Now: no delays. It will keep nagging until you mark it complete. 

Then: you could mark complete from the lock screen. 
Now: you must go into the app to mark complete. 

Please bring back the practical features of this app!

title: A free native app that is feature packed
body:
I’ve tried all the major task management apps out there - Things3, Todoisy, TickTick, Any.do, and probably a dozen others. Yet I use apple reminders. 

Apple reminders is incredibly feature rich, with features that rival app that cost a considerable amount of money each year. The ability to easily attach items, set location-based reminders, and share lists is indispensable for me and those features are not universally included in other apps (or they don’t work consistently). 

With tags and lists it’s very easy to make reminders work exactly how you want it. In addition, apple reminders works with a number of other apps including fantastical, agenda, and GoodTask. 

I always recommend Apple Reminders as a task manager for people who need one.

title: Not Apple’s best effort!
body: I’ve been using the Reminders app for several years now. And for all that time, I’ve kept hoping for sorely needed improvements that still have not come as of iOS 15. First, it’s very slow to reflect updates to my reminders. I used to think the slowness was due to my slow internet connection in our rural area. But I’ve also seen the same behavior when connected to fast broadband at my son’s house. Second, it’s unreliable. If I click on a reminder that it’s complete, I don’t want to have to worry whether or not that entry has been implemented properly. But that’s exactly what happens constantly. If I click an item as complete, I then have to spend the time to watch as the open circle at the left is filled in blue, then usually the blue disappears and the circle becomes clear again before the item is moved to the next day or week or month depending on the repeat setting. Additionally, I have to look at the next day, week or month to verify that the reminder was indeed moved to that place. Many times it is not updated correctly, and I have to manually correct the next occurrence of the reminder item. Third, the syncing between the iPhone Reminder app and the similar software on my iMac, MacBook Pro, and Apple Watch stinks. Typically if I click on an item as complete on my iPhone, and then go to use my iMac, it invariably puts up a notification that that same reminder item is still open and gives me choices about what to do with it. If I tell Reminders that a repeating item is complete through my Apple Watch, it often shows up in Reminders on my iPhone or iMac as being moved two days, weeks or months ahead for the next occurrence instead of one. Again, I have to manually correct things. I want to like Reminders and do use it for some time-critical things like when to take medicines, when payments are due, etc. But if I could find a suitable replacement for Reminders, I would switch to it without hesitation.

title: iOS15 = great updates!! (4.5 🌟)
body:
I'm a hard-core To Do List person, maintaining a digital one for over 20 years. So, I love high-functionality, but I also love simplicity of use. Apple has moved closer to both in their iOS15 iteration of Reminders. 

For all those who think they lost functionality, long-press on the notification. Mark as completed, and remind me later... are still options.

iOS15 brings TAGGING! Which completely revolutionizes the functionality of this app. Along with smart lists & easy conversions, plus (as before) shared tasks, location-based reminders, siri integration, also integrations with other productivity apps, it truly (finally) makes iOS Reminders a major player in the field. 4-stars only because there's still a bit of work to be done on advanced features to rank it up there with the strongest of the bunch, but this app is now truly functional for the majority of folks needing a handy todo list. 

If you found this review helpful, please tap and hold to mark helpful, so others can see it, as well. Thanks!
